<backstage_guidance>
Choose Owen's interview as the main developing personal thread for the next day. He wants this opportunity and intends to accept before Wednesday noon. His Thursday-to-Friday swap is approved in principle; the written request and Nell's confirmation still need to happen. Let him take those steps himself. His difficulty is telling Martin what the opportunity means when Martin has begun imagining a settled future together at the cinema. Give that relationship room to change through something Owen or Martin actually does. Do not assume an interview result or a decision to leave town.

This is direction for future action, not a report that these things have happened. Rowan and Nell know only about an inland appointment; Jo knows the interview, and Martin has not been told. A disclosure must come from someone who can make it. If Rowan meets Owen, Owen can decide what he wants to share; do not make the encounter or a confession compulsory. Offstage decisions can become visible later through their consequences, without a report of every private conversation.

Let the reopening also mean a life people want to have. Jo wants time with Fran and misses Ines; Nell wants the booked walking weekend with Gina. Their immediate business can reveal a preference or decision serving those lives, rather than only another duty. If Bea is naturally at lunch, her answer can draw on the films, possessions and people she cares about. They need not all appear, and Rowan need not help. Use the full histories to choose what matters to the people who are actually present.

Resolve the existing practical clock: Dev's Tuesday evening hold required confirmation by noon today. Establish the outcome consistently if it becomes relevant; Rosa's completed photographs and her evening with Beth do not need to be disrupted. These are opportunities for independent progress, not errands for Rowan or a required sequence of scenes.
</backstage_guidance>

Return the next passage of fiction.

At lunch, if Bea is present, I ask what she enjoys about having the cinema open again. If she is not here, I eat with whoever is around.
</user>

summary: **Staging Owen's lunch with Nell and Rowan**

item.text:
At half past twelve, you take your lunch downstairs. Bea is not in the building. Nell and Owen occupy one of the cafe tables, with the office diary open between them.

Yesterday’s pencilled auditorium hold has been replaced in ink:

**DEV / HANA — RECEIVER TEST — 19.00–19.30**  
**confirmed 11.20**

Owen has a packed lunch open beside his phone. Nell finishes reading something on hers and looks across at him.

“Your email came through. Thursday’s shift is moved to Friday, ten until four. I’ve updated the rota.”

“Thanks.” Owen unlocks his phone. “Then I can answer this.”

He types for a moment before setting the phone face down.

“I’ve accepted the interview. Thursday at eleven.”

Nell’s pen stops over the diary. “The inland appointment?”

“It’s a permanent exhibition-technician job at a museum. Or it might be. At the moment it’s only an interview.”

“I didn’t know you’d applied.”

“I’ve been looking for something longer-term that uses the work I’m trained for.”

Nell nods. “The shift change is confirmed. If anything else changes, tell me when it does.”

Owen glances towards the foyer, although Martin is nowhere in sight.

“Jo knows about the interview. Dad doesn’t. I want him to hear it from me.”

Nell closes the rota. “I won’t mention it.”

Owen looks briefly towards you, no longer concealing what he has chosen to say in your presence.

“He’s started talking as if I’ll still be working here after this contract. I haven’t promised that. I haven’t been offered anything either.”

Nobody asks you to interpret the difference for Martin.

After a few minutes, Nell opens the diary to October and blocks out the ninth through the eleventh.

“Gina’s booked our walking weekend,” she says. “I’m taking those days as leave. I’ll arrange the manager cover before the rota goes out.”

The dates remain marked in ink while the three of you finish lunch.
